guidance: The page cannot read the receiver: the semitones it reports assume the bend range you enter matches the range the instrument or plug-in is actually set to, usually through RPN 0. Check the patch before relying on the interval.
method: A pitch bend change is sent as the status byte 1110nnnn for the channel followed by the seven-bit least-significant byte and the seven-bit most-significant byte of a fourteen-bit value, so the value is MSB x 128 + LSB. Centre is 8192 (2000H) and means no pitch change. The pitch offset is (value - 8192) / 8192 x bend range, so a value of 0 is the whole range down, 16383 is 8191/8192 of the range up, and the cents are the offset x 100 with the frequency ratio 2^(semitones/12). Going the other way, the value is 8192 + (offset / range) x 8192, rounded to the nearest whole number and clamped to 0 to 16383, and the page reports how far that rounded value sits from the requested offset in cents. The bend range must be 0.01 to 127 semitones, the range RPN 0 can carry, written with at most two decimal places; the channel must be 1 to 16 and a bend value must be a whole number from 0 to 16383. Blank, malformed and out-of-range entries are refused with the failing field named instead of being defaulted. The page models the message and the arithmetic only: it does not read or send MIDI, and it cannot know whether a device honours the least-significant byte, uses a different range, or supports the resulting interval.

sources.title: Table 1 — Summary of MIDI 1.0 Messages: Pitch Bend Change is a fourteen-bit value, centre 2000H, LSB then MSB, sensitivity set by RPN 0 (MIDI Association)
